the immobilization of methemoglobin into nanoparticulate Ti(2)O(3) thin films leads to the formation of a redox-active species that undergoes two distinct electrochemical reduction processes.
The electrochemical reduction (reversible) of methemoglobin in nanoparticulate anatase TiO2 films is observed in two voltammetric steps.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrochemical properties of methemoglobin in a TiO(2)-host and the influence of electrochemical conductivity of the host on the electrochemical reduction of the guest.
the development of new types of thin film electrodes that are capable of reversible electrochemical reactions of redox active proteins.
a new class of thin film materials that can be used to immobilize redox-active proteins and to control their redox chemistry by means of electrochemical doping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electrochemical doping is a reversible phenomenon which can be used to switch between reversible and irreversible electron transfer in a TiO(2)-based system.
the electrochemical behavior of methemoglobin in nanoparticulate films of TiO(,2) is strongly influenced by the conductivity and electrochemical dopability of the host.
the electrochemical reduction of immobilized methemoglobin in porous TiO2 films is observed in two processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduction of methoglobin immobilized in porous TiO2 can be electrochemically controlled and the electrochemical response can be enhanced by the application of negative potentials.
the electrochemical doping of nanoparticulate Ti(2) films leads to a considerable enhancement of electron transfer to immobilized methemoglobin.
we have demonstrated that the reduction of methamoglobin immobilized in thin porous TiO2 films is possible and that the electrochemical doping of TiO2 can enhance the rate of this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrochemical reduction of the heme group in methemoglobin immobilised in TiO( 2) films can be switched on/off by the application of an external potential.

the reversible reduction of methemoglobiin in the TiO( 2) film occurs only at the surface and that the reduction of methhemoglobin at potentials more positive than the flat band potential of TiO( 1) is not a bulk process.
